newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Sweden bank sector heats up with merger deals.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Sweden bank sector heats up with merger deals.

text.p: The restructuring of Sweden's bank sector picked up speed on Monday with Swedbank and Foreningsbanken announcing merger talks and Handelsbanken finalising a takeover of Stadshypotek.
Two weeks after merger talks between S-E-Banken and Nordbanken collapsed, interest in the sector heated up again with Swedbank and Foreningsbanken confirming market rumours of a possible merger.
"We hereby confirm ongoing discussions between the two institutions as to a potential merger," the two banks said in a statement.
The Stockholm bourse suspended trading in the banks which said more information would be released at 0845 GMT on Tuesday.
The bank sector jumped in morning trade, rising 1.01 percent against a general index gain of 0.24 percent.
Over the past year the sector has been rife with talk of restructuring as Swedish banks prepare to face increased competition from larger, European banks.
A possible partnership of Foreningsbanken and Swedbank was first mooted last June when Swedbank took a five percent slice in the smaller bank that has a large rural customer base.
But Foreningsbanken's key shareholders, farmers' associations which hold a 20.1 percent stake, spurned the advances of Swedbank -- known in Sweden as Sparbanken -- saying it would not be beneficial.
The farmers' associations have not commented on the current talks.

Swedbank, which has a market capitalisation of 30 billion crowns ($4.1 billion), closed at 119.5 crowns on Friday while Foreningsbanken, which has a market capitalisation of seven billion crowns, last traded at 38.50 crowns.
Both are due to release 1996 earnings this week.

Analysts said they expected a mixed market reaction on any deal. "Swedbank's share should rise somewhat, while Foreningsbanken's share price to some extent includes a bid," said Fredrik Myren, analyst at James Capel in Stockholm.

But the announcement was greeted positively. "It's quite good news," said James Alexander, analyst at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson. "The banks have similar cultures and they should get scope for savings."
The surge of interest in the bank sector was not just confined to a possible marriage of Swedbank and Foreningsbank.
The day began with Sweden's largest bank by assets, Handelsbanken, announcing its purchase of Sweden's largest mortgage lender, Stadshypotek, had been completed.

The 22.9 billion crown cash takeover bid, which was launched last December and quashed a merger proposal by insurer Skandia, was conditional on Handelsbanken receiving at least 90 percent of Stadshypotek.

"Counting of the outcome has not yet been completed but it is already clear that Handelsbanken will own over 98 percent of shares," the bank said in a statement. "The outcome exceeds all expectations."
Handelsbanken shares benefited from the announcement and the increased interest in banks, rising four crowns to 197 crowns.

Analysts said the possible merger of Swedbank and Foreningsbanken was likely to re-ignite interest in S-E-Banken and state-controlled Nordbanken. "This will put some pressure on Nordbanken and S-E-Banken that will be the only large banks not involved in a deal," said Myren.
